ai.name: Anthropic
ai.hook: Claude Opus 5 launches, matching Fable 5 on coding at half the price.
insights: Scored an **ECI of 159** vs Fable 5's 161, but matched it on software engineering benchmarks
Boris Cherny (Anthropic): Opus 5 is their **least prompt-injectable model yet**, per red-teaming in the system card
Odd quirk: performs better at **medium effort than high effort** on FrontierCode benchmark
ai.for_you: If you're building agents for PT SMB clients that touch client data or forms, the prompt-injection resistance is the actual headline, not the benchmark score, since that's what breaks in production, not lab evals.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Biggest model release of the week, top HN story at 1533pts

ai.name: Ars Technica
ai.hook: Opus 5 is a token-efficiency play, not a capability leap, per closer analysis.
insights: Anthropic's own framing: '**thoughtful and proactive**, close to Fable 5 frontier intelligence at half the price**'
Coding-agent capability praised by users as 'incredibly underrated' despite modest benchmark delta
ai.for_you: Cheaper-but-almost-as-good is exactly the economics you want for agency client work: run Opus 5 as your default coding/agent backend and reserve Fable-tier models only for tasks that truly need max reasoning.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Best counter-narrative to the Opus 5 hype cycle

ai.name: Black Forest Labs
ai.hook: FLUX 3 unifies image, video, audio and action prediction in one model.
insights: Beats **Seedance 2.0, Gemini Omni, and Grok Imagine** on multimodal benchmarks
**FLUX-mimic** spinoff demonstrates general-purpose robotics dexterity running on a **single GPU**
ai.for_you: Worth testing FLUX 3 for the yoga platform: one model for generating class thumbnails, short promo video clips, and voiceover audio instead of stitching three separate tools together.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Only major non-LLM model release this week

ai.name: Interconnects
ai.hook: Open-weight models face their most serious viability test yet, says '6 months to live'.
insights: **Kimi K3** ranks top on agentic and frontend tasks, escalating the open-weights race
**GLM-5.2** marked as a genuine capability step-change for open agents
US policy is moving toward **procurement restrictions** and possible Entity List designation for Chinese open models
ai.for_you: If your agency stack leans on open-weight models for cost reasons with PT clients, watch this closely: a US Entity List move on Kimi/GLM could force a scramble to re-platform mid-contract.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Most substantive ongoing policy thread affecting open-model access

ai.name: Martin Alderson / HN commentary
ai.hook: OpenAI's rogue-agent story looks less like a stunt, more like exposed enormous attack surface.
insights: Hugging Face's attack surface is called '**enormous**' by design given it runs arbitrary user code at scale
Thomas Ptacek: any 2025-era open-weights model with a pentest harness could likely pull off similar sandbox escapes on most networks
Guardian piece urges skepticism (485pts, 280 comments on HN) about the framing of the incident
ai.for_you: No direct action here, filed for awareness, this only matters if you're deploying agents with real filesystem/network access for a client, which you're not doing yet.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Highest-engagement security story of the week, multiple outlets converging

ai.name: Eiso Kant
ai.hook: Poolside runs 10,000-20,000 training experiments a month via its 'Model Factory'.
insights: Spent **4 years and $12M** on code-focused LLMs before the market cared
Believes **persistence, verification, and backtracking** matter more than raw model intelligence
Argues for 100 foundation model companies over 5, even if Poolside is one of the 5
ai.for_you: The 'persistence and verification over raw intelligence' framing is directly useful for how you scope agentic workflows for SMB clients: build in retry/verify loops rather than betting on a smarter single-shot model.
ai.why_it_made_the_cut: Best long-form builder insight of the week, not just a headline

build_this.name: Claude Cookbook
build_this.what_it_is: Anthropic's official collection of practical Claude implementation recipes and patterns.
build_this.why_try_it: Pull the agentic/tool-use recipes directly into your agency's client delivery templates this week, it's the fastest way to standardize how you build Claude-based workflows for PT SMBs without reinventing prompts each time.

build_this.name: FLUX 3 / FLUX-mimic
build_this.source: Black Forest Labs via Latent Space
build_this.what_it_is: Unified multimodal model generating image, video, audio, and action in one pass.
build_this.why_try_it: Test it this week for the yoga platform: generate a class trailer (visual + voiceover) from a single prompt instead of juggling separate image, TTS, and video tools, could cut your content production time significantly.

build_this.name: paperless-ngx
build_this.what_it_is: Self-hosted document management system that scans, OCRs, and indexes documents automatically.
build_this.why_try_it: Portuguese SMBs drown in paper invoices and contracts, this is a ready-made backend you could white-label or wire into an AI agency offer for automated document intake plus a Claude layer for extraction and categorization.
